standards.name: Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD)
standards.summary: Sets which organisations must publish a sustainability report and how that report is assured. Research organisations and operators in scope use it to plan what the baseline must be ready to evidence.

standards.name: European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS)
standards.summary: The reporting standards under the CSRD. They describe the environmental and governance disclosures a datacenter, research infrastructure, or organisation may need to prepare.

standards.name: Energy Efficiency Directive (EED)
standards.summary: EU rules on energy efficiency, including reporting expectations for large energy users and datacenters. Useful when the baseline covers energy management and disclosure.

standards.name: Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation (ESPR)
standards.summary: Sets ecodesign and product-information rules for goods placed on the EU market. Relevant when procurement and equipment choices are part of the baseline.

standards.name: Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment Directive (WEEE)
standards.summary: Rules for collecting and treating waste electrical equipment. It guides end-of-life handling of IT and datacenter equipment.

standards.name: ISO 14001
standards.summary: Environmental management system standard. It is the usual reference for how a research infrastructure or organisation runs environmental policy, roles, and improvement.

standards.name: ISO 14040 and ISO 14044
standards.summary: Life-cycle assessment principles and requirements. Use them when the baseline looks at impacts across design, operation, and end of life.

standards.name: ISO 14006
standards.summary: Guidelines for bringing environmental aspects into design. Relevant for equipment, services, and facilities that are still being specified.

standards.name: ISO 14024
standards.summary: Principles for Type I environmental labels. It helps when procurement looks for independently certified products.

standards.name: ISO 14031
standards.summary: Guidance on environmental performance evaluation. It supports choosing indicators and checking whether the recorded level is backed by measurement.

standards.name: ISO 14046
standards.summary: Water-footprint principles and requirements. Use it when cooling water or site water use is in the baseline.

standards.name: ISO 14063
standards.summary: Guidance on environmental communication. It is the reference for how results and claims are explained to partners and the public.

standards.name: ISO 14064
standards.summary: Greenhouse-gas quantification and reporting at organisation level. It sits beside the GHG Protocol when the baseline includes a carbon inventory.

standards.name: ISO 20400
standards.summary: Guidance on sustainable procurement. It helps a research organisation or operator set expectations for suppliers and purchased services.

standards.name: ISO 50001
standards.summary: Energy management system standard. It is the usual reference for a structured approach to energy performance in facilities and datacenters.

standards.name: ISO/IEC 30134
standards.summary: Key performance indicators for datacenters, including power and water metrics. It applies where the organisation runs or specifies datacenter capacity.

standards.name: EN 50600
standards.summary: European series for datacenter facilities and their environmental key performance indicators. It guides design and operation of on-prem and colocation sites.

standards.name: EU Code of Conduct for Data Centre Energy Efficiency
standards.summary: A voluntary European code of expected energy-efficiency practices for datacenters. Participants use it as a practical checklist beside the baseline.

standards.name: EMAS
standards.summary: The EU eco-management and audit scheme. An organisation can use it when it wants a verified environmental management system and a public statement.

standards.name: GHG Protocol
standards.summary: The common method for corporate greenhouse-gas inventories, including purchased electricity. It is the usual companion to carbon figures in the baseline.

standards.name: Renewable Energy Directive
standards.summary: EU rules on renewable energy targets and claims. Relevant when the baseline records renewable electricity or renewable heat.

standards.name: Electricity Directive
standards.summary: EU rules for the electricity market, including how consumers take part. It is background for power-sourcing and flexibility topics.

standards.name: EU Green Public Procurement
standards.summary: Voluntary EU criteria for buying goods and services with a lower environmental impact. Research organisations use them when tenders need a sustainability clause.

standards.name: EU Circular Economy Action Plan
standards.summary: The EU policy frame for keeping products and materials in use. It guides waste, reuse, and procurement topics in the baseline.

standards.name: Industrial Emissions Directive
standards.summary: EU rules on pollution prevention for industrial installations. It is a reference when a site has permitted emissions or significant local pollution control.

standards.name: Water Framework Directive
standards.summary: The EU framework for protecting rivers, lakes, and groundwater. It is the policy context for water withdrawal and discharge at a site.

standards.name: EU Biodiversity Strategy for 2030
standards.summary: The EU strategy for restoring nature. It is the context for land, habitat, and site-ecology topics in a research campus or facility baseline.

standards.name: EU Taxonomy
standards.summary: The EU classification of economic activities that can count as environmentally sustainable. It matters when a report or investment case needs a taxonomy alignment statement.
